Hair Services

Hair Treatments: An Overview

Home / Hair Services / Hair Treatments

Between cuts and color, treatments are the services aimed specifically at hair health — repairing damage, adding moisture, or temporarily changing texture. They're often add-on services rather than standalone appointments, but understanding what each one actually does helps you decide which, if any, are worth booking for your hair.

Deep Conditioning

Deep conditioning treatments use concentrated moisturizing formulas, often with heat, to temporarily improve softness and manageability in dry or damaged hair. Heat helps open the hair's outer cuticle layer slightly so conditioning ingredients can penetrate more effectively than a standard rinse-out conditioner would achieve on its own. Results are noticeable but temporary — deep conditioning improves the condition of existing hair, it doesn't repair damage permanently, since hair itself can't truly heal once it's structurally damaged.

Smoothing Treatments

Smoothing treatments aim to reduce frizz and simplify styling for a period of weeks to months. Formulas and results vary widely — some soften and relax the hair's natural texture without fully straightening it, while others produce a much straighter result that lasts longer. Ask your stylist to explain the specific product and process they use, including how it will affect curl pattern, since some smoothing treatments are more permanent in their effect on texture than others and that's an important distinction before committing.

Bond-Building Treatments

A newer category of in-salon treatment focuses on rebuilding the internal bonds within the hair shaft that get broken down by chemical processing — particularly lightening. These are often added alongside a color service rather than booked separately, and are aimed at reducing breakage during and after a chemical process rather than adding shine or softness on their own.

Scalp Treatments

Some salons also offer scalp-focused treatments — exfoliation, massage, or targeted serums meant to support a healthy scalp environment for hair growth. These are generally cosmetic and relaxation-focused services. They are not a substitute for medical care, and any persistent scalp irritation, unusual hair loss, or itching should be evaluated by a dermatologist rather than treated with salon services alone.

General Considerations

Treatments are generally cosmetic and temporary rather than a permanent fix, and the honest answer to "will this fix my damaged hair" is usually "it will improve how it looks and feels for now." For scalp conditions, hair loss, or other medical concerns, consult a dermatologist or qualified healthcare professional rather than relying on a salon treatment, however well-marketed.

Deciding What's Worth Adding

If your hair feels dry or brittle after a lightening service, a bond-building or deep-conditioning add-on is usually a reasonable investment. If your main complaint is everyday frizz rather than damage, a smoothing treatment may be the better fit — but ask specifically how long results last and how it will affect future color services, since some smoothing chemicals interact with color processing.

Treatments Aren't a Substitute for Basic Care

It's worth remembering that in-salon treatments work best as a supplement to a solid at-home routine, not a replacement for one. Skipping heat protectant or sulfate-free shampoo at home and relying on an occasional salon treatment to compensate tends to be a losing trade — the daily habits matter more, cumulatively, than any single periodic treatment, however effective that treatment is in the moment.

How Often to Book a Treatment

There's no universal schedule, but a reasonable starting point is a deep conditioning or bond-building treatment every four to six weeks for chemically treated hair, and less frequently — every couple of months — for hair that isn't regularly colored or lightened. Let how your hair actually feels guide the schedule more than a fixed calendar; hair that still feels soft and manageable doesn't necessarily need a treatment just because time has passed.
